requirements.quote:
The BGP protocol allows for multiple address prefixes with the same
   path attributes to be specified in one message.
requirements.condition: Multiple address prefixes share the same path attributes.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit multiple such address prefixes to be specified in one message.
requirements.why_checkable: The message encoder and decoder can be checked for support of multiple prefixes under one path attribute set.

requirements.quote:
The BGP protocol allows for multiple address prefixes with the same
   path attributes to be specified in one message.  Using this
   capability is highly recommended.
requirements.condition: Advertising multiple address prefixes with the same path attributes.
requirements.required_behavior: Combining these prefixes in one message is highly recommended.
requirements.why_checkable: Advertisement batching can be inspected while preserving its recommendation strength.

requirements.quote:
As each address prefix is processed, a
   message for the associated set of path attributes is allocated, if it
   does not exist, and the new address prefix is added to it.
requirements.condition: If using the described optional routing-table scanning method, a prefix is processed and no message for its path attribute set exists.
requirements.required_behavior: Allocate a message for the associated path attribute set.
requirements.why_checkable: The optional batching algorithm has an observable allocation branch.

requirements.quote:
As each address prefix is processed, a
   message for the associated set of path attributes is allocated, if it
   does not exist, and the new address prefix is added to it.
requirements.condition: If using the described optional routing-table scanning method, a message has just been allocated for the prefix's path attribute set.
requirements.required_behavior: Add the new address prefix to that message.
requirements.why_checkable: The newly created message can be checked for the triggering prefix.

requirements.quote:
If such a
   message exists, the new address prefix is appended to it.
requirements.condition: If using the described optional batching method, a message for the path attribute set already exists and has room for the prefix.
requirements.required_behavior: Append the new address prefix to that message.
requirements.why_checkable: The existing-message branch can be checked for prefix accumulation.

requirements.quote:
If the
   message lacks the space to hold the new address prefix, it is
   transmitted, a new message is allocated, and the new address prefix
   is inserted into the new message.
requirements.condition: If using the described optional batching method, the current message lacks space for the next address prefix.
requirements.why_checkable: The capacity branch has a directly observable send action.

requirements.quote:
If the
   message lacks the space to hold the new address prefix, it is
   transmitted, a new message is allocated, and the new address prefix
   is inserted into the new message.
requirements.condition: If using the described optional batching method, a full message has been transmitted because the next prefix would not fit.
requirements.why_checkable: The capacity branch can be inspected for allocation of a replacement message.

requirements.quote:
If the
   message lacks the space to hold the new address prefix, it is
   transmitted, a new message is allocated, and the new address prefix
   is inserted into the new message.
requirements.condition: If using the described optional batching method, a replacement message has been allocated after the previous message lacked space for the prefix.
requirements.required_behavior: Insert the new address prefix into the replacement message.
requirements.why_checkable: The overflow prefix can be checked for inclusion in the replacement message.

requirements.quote:
When the entire routing table has
   been scanned, all allocated messages are sent and their resources are
   released.
requirements.condition: If using the described optional batching method, the entire routing table has been scanned.
requirements.why_checkable: End-of-scan flushing can be checked against the pending message set.

requirements.quote:
When the entire routing table has
   been scanned, all allocated messages are sent and their resources are
   released.
requirements.condition: If using the described optional batching method, the entire routing table has been scanned and allocated messages have been sent.
requirements.required_behavior: Release the resources of the allocated messages.
requirements.why_checkable: Resource ownership after flushing can be checked.

requirements.quote: One method of doing this is to limit the rate of updates.
requirements.condition: When peering with an implementation that sends separate messages for address prefixes, if choosing the described optional overhead-reduction method.
requirements.why_checkable: The optional method maps to an inspectable update-rate control.

requirements.quote:
A better
   method would be to read all received messages before sending updates.
requirements.condition: When reducing overhead from a peer that does not compress multiple address prefixes into one message.
requirements.required_behavior: Reading all received messages before sending updates is suggested as the better method.
requirements.why_checkable: Receive processing and outbound-update ordering are observable; this is advisory, not mandatory.
